DAMGHANI:v1p18/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r6.claim: Aḥad can refer to God in the statement that He sees.
DAMGHANI:v1p18/r6.anchor: احد يعني الله تعالى قوله في سورة البلد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r4.claim: Verses 5–7 rebuke people who claim they have spent a fortune: they should have thanked God and aided the needy, but think He does not see their wasteful spending.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r4.anchor: As an obligation towards these favours and blessings of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r2.claim: Conceit that wealth and status were self-earned or a birthright leaves people unwilling to spend for God and indifferent to Him and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r2.anchor: spend in the way of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r3.claim: To excuse miserliness, such people recite their many personal and collective expenses and challenge callers to say how much more they should give.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r3.anchor: long list of expenditures and try to prove to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r4.claim: The expression mālan lubadā means a great amount of wealth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r5.claim: God sees the truth behind their boast: they spend nothing yet claim generosity, and their supposed spending will be fully exposed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p322/r5.anchor: no one is observing their generosity

NAHHAS:v5p229/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p229/r5.claim: The original is yarʾahu; hamza's vowel shifts to rāʾ, then hamza drops because it becomes quiescent beside another quiescent consonant.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r5.anchor: والأصل يرأه قلبت حركة الهمزة على الراء فانفتحت وسقطت الهمزة

NAHHAS:v5p229/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p229/r6.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v5p229/r6.claim: Asked why the hamza disappears after its vowel shifts, he explains that the newly quiescent hamza follows a rāʾ given only an incidental vowel, so it is deleted before the next consonant.
NAHHAS:v5p229/r6.anchor: سألته عنه قال لما سقطت حركة الهمزة وسكنت وكانت الراء قبلها ساكنة فحركت حركة عارضة فكان حكمها حكم الساكن وبعدها ساكن فحذف ما بعدها وهو الهمزة

DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.claim: He identified the father as Adam, offspring as his children, hardship as severity, labad as much, and ‘does he think no one sees’ as no one can overpower him.
DURR-FULL:v8p519/r5.anchor: وأخرج الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

DURR-FULL:v8p520/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r12.speaker: رجل من بني عامر
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r12.claim: A man who prayed behind the Prophet heard him recite the two questions as ‘does he think none can overpower him?’ and ‘does he think no one saw him?’ with yaḥsab opened.
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r12.anchor: وأخرج أبو يعلى والبغوي وابن مردويه عن رجل من بني عامر رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v8p520/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r13.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r13.claim: He said the disbeliever thinks God cannot overpower him or see him.
DURR-FULL:v8p520/r13.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن السدي رضي الله عنه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r4.claim: Mujahid takes the question about being seen to mean that the person thinks no one can overpower him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3433/r4.anchor: ايحسب ان لم يره أحد قال : لم يقدر عليه أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.claim: The next lines expose the boast of wasteful spending as a false virtue among pre-Islamic Arabs; the cited ʿAntara poem boasts of spending wealth while preserving honor, and the statement is a circumstantial description of the human's hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p351/r6.anchor: أعقبت مساوي نفسه بمذام أقواله ، وهو التفخر الكاذب والتمدح بإتلاف المال في غير صلاح .

MUQATIL:90:5-16/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r2.claim: God sees and counts what a person spends and will replace it for them.
MUQATIL:90:5-16/r2.anchor: { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } [آية: 7] أو يحسب هذا الإنسان أن الله تعالى ليس يرى

ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r8.claim: He thinks no one saw him means he thinks no one recorded his spending; his claim suggests that he said he spent much without benefit.
ZAJJAJ:v5p327#2/r8.anchor: أي أيحسب أن لم يحص عليه ما أنفق، وفي الكلام دليل

TABATABAI:90:4-10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r5.claim: Boasting of vast spending implies imagining God did not see it; God sees what was spent, but spending alone is insufficient without harder acts of servitude and solidarity with believers.
TABATABAI:90:4-10/r5.anchor: أن لازم إخبار الإنسان بإهلاكه مالا لبدا أنه يحسب أنا في غفلة وجهل بما أنفق

TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r2.claim: The question asks whether the person thinks God did not see him and will not demand an account of his income and spending.
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r2.anchor: أحد } فيطالبه من أين اكتسبه وفي ماذا أنفقه عن قتادة

TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says every servant will be questioned about lifespan, wealth earned and spent, deeds, and love for the Prophet's family.
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r4.claim: The man may have lied about spending; God saw whether or not he actually spent it.
TABRISI:90:1-20#4/r4.anchor: إنه كان كاذبا لم ينفق ما قاله فقال الله سبحانه أيظن أن الله تعالى لم ير ذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r2.claim: The question asks whether the spender thinks his actions and motives are hidden; God knows whether he spent anything, lied, and why he spent it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r2.anchor: فالله يعلم إن كان أنفق مالاً أو لم ينفق شيئاً، وإن كان مدّعياً كاذباً في قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r3.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r3.claim: The watched one in the verse may be God, who sees the person and acts as his watcher.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r3.anchor: يعني أن الله كان يراه وكان عليه رقيباً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r4.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf also allows the pronoun to refer to the human being.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r5.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r5.claim: The question can mean that he thinks his deeds and spending motives are concealed from everyone and not for God's sake.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p261/r5.anchor: أَيحسبُ أن أعماله تَخْفى، وأنه لا يراه أحد، ولا يطّلع عليه في إنفاقه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r2.claim: God saw his spending and knows its amount.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:90:6-13/r2.anchor: { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } في إنفاقه، فيعلم مقدار نفقته

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r13.claim: The question warns that God saw the spendthrift’s acts, will punish him for wasteful display or enmity, and he will regret it.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r13.anchor: Şüphe yok ki sarf ve ihlâk ettiyse onu Ehad olan Allah teâlâ görmüştür

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r14.speaker: Kelbî
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r14.claim: Al-Kalbi also reads the question as exposing a lie: the man claims to have spent much but spent nothing, and God knows what he truly did.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r14.anchor: Kelbî’den rivayet edildiği üzere sarf iddiasını tekzibdir

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r15.claim: Elmalılı prefers the warning interpretation because it can also imply that the boast was false.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r15.anchor: Evvelki vecih, bu mânayı da işrab edebileceği için daha müfiddir

ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.claim: God’s gifts guide humanity toward its purpose and establish divine knowledge and power to reckon and punish; the contrast between tranquil and unbelieving souls further explains hardship.
ELMALILI:90:3-7#3/r16.anchor: halkettiği insana ve bu meyanda bilhassa kuvvet ve malıyla iftihar eden

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r7.claim: God saw the man's spending and knew his corrupt intention, and will judge it; ostentatious spending is a vice mistaken by the ignorant for virtue.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r7.anchor: يعني إن الله رآه واطلع على خبث نيته وفساد سريرته وإنه مجازيه عليه

QASHANI:90:5-7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:5-7/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:5-7/r3.claim: He wrongly assumes God did not see his inner motive: spending for reputation, vanity, and boasting rather than God’s pleasure compounds vice instead of making virtue.
QASHANI:90:5-7/r3.anchor: أيحسب أن لم يطلع الله تعالى على باطنه ونيته حين ينفق ماله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says the man spent heaps of money obstructing God's path, and the one he thinks did not see him is God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : اهلكت مالا لبدا قال : انفقت مالا في الصد عن سبيل الله ايحسب ان لم يره أحد قال : الاحد : الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r1.claim: The question about whether anyone saw him elaborates on his claim to have spent much wealth: he assumes everyone will believe a boast that some people can recognize as false.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r1.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { يقول أهلكت مالا } لأن قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r2.speaker: زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r2.claim: Zuhayr's verse says a person's character becomes known even if he thinks it is hidden from people, supporting the claim that the boaster's lie is observable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r2.anchor:
قال زهير :
ومهما تكن عند امرىء من خليقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r3.claim: The interrogative rebukes and denies his assumption, indirectly asserting God's knowledge of his inner motives and exposing his false boast of generosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r3.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار وتوبيخ وهو كناية عن علم الله تعالى بدخيلته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.claim: The next verses explain the rebuke: the creator of human perception and speech must know and be able to judge people's acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.anchor: فكيف يكون مفيض العلم على الناس غير قادر وغير عالم بأحوالهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r8.claim: The named person falsely boasts of spending wealth, so “does he think no one saw him?” means his action was seen and recorded; on the generic reading it asks whether he thinks no recording angels watch him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r8.anchor: أيحسب أن لم يره أحد أي أنه رئي وأحصي فعله فما باله يكذب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r9.claim: A prophetic report says a servant's feet will not move until he is asked about his life, body, and the source and expenditure of his wealth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r9.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تزول قدما عبد حتى يسأل عن عمره فيما أفناه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r11.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r11.claim: Al-A'mash reads lam yarahu with sukūn on rāʾ to avoid successive short vowels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p484/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: «لم يره» بسكون الراء لتوالي الحركات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p131/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p131/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p131/r1.claim: God saw and recorded his expenditure; the man had claimed to spend more than he actually did.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p131/r1.anchor: يعني الله عز وجل والمعنى أيظن أن الله لم ير نفقته ولم يحصها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r5.claim: Mujahid and other early interpreters say the person thinks God did not see him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p404/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: أي أيحسب أن لم يره الله عز وجل. وكذا قال غيره من السلف.

FARRA:v3p263/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p263/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p263/r11.claim: He claimed he had spent much wealth opposing Muhammad, but this was a lie; God saw what he spent.
FARRA:v3p263/r11.anchor:
والله قادر عليه.
ثم قال: يقول:
أنفقت مالا كثيرا في عداوة محمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.claim: The person questioned is a Quraysh notable who assumes there will be no Resurrection or retribution despite his strength and mistreatment of believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r3.anchor: أيظن هذا الصنديد القوي في قومه المتضعف للمؤمنين : أن لن تقوم قيامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r5.claim: God saw and watched him when he spent for public display and boasting.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p758/r5.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاء الناس وافتخارا بينهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r15.claim: He says the person thinks God did not see what he spent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r15.anchor: أن لم يره الله , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r16.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r16.claim: He says the person thinks no one among people saw what he spent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p276/r17.claim: A further reading is a threat: the person thinks no one will expose or punish what he did; the other readings refute his claim.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#5/r1.claim: He assumes no one saw his spending, which he did ostentatiously for reputation; God saw it and watched over him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#5/r1.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رياه وافتخارا يعنى أن الله تعالى كان يراه وكان عليه رقيبا

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r3.claim: The man falsely assumes no one witnessed his spending; God saw him, and he had not actually spent what he claimed.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r3.anchor: بل علم الله عز وجل ذلك منه، فكان كاذبا في قوله: أهلكت

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.claim: God knows and can reckon his conduct; the eyes, tongue, and lips recall divine favor and God’s ability to resurrect and account for deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.anchor: ألم يعلم أن الله قادر على محاسبته، وأن الله عز وجل يرى صنيعه، ثم عدد عليه نعمه

QUTB-ZILAL:90:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:7/r1.claim: God sees both what a person spends and why; the deluded person wrongly imagines he is hidden from God's sight.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:7/r1.anchor: فهو يرى ما أنفق ،  ولماذا أنفق

RAZI:90:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:7/r1.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:90:7/r1.claim: Qatāda reads the verse as asking whether the person thinks God has not seen him or will not ask how he earned and spent his wealth.
RAZI:90:7/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : أيظن أن الله لم يره ولم يسأله عن ماله من أين اكتسبه

RAZI:90:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:7/r2.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:90:7/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says the man lied and gave nothing; God saw whether he gave or withheld and knew that his claim was false.
RAZI:90:7/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي : كان كاذبا لم ينفق شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says the person assumes God neither saw nor will ask how he earned and spent his money.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : أيظن أن الله لم / يره ولم يسأله عن ماله من أين اكتسبه وفيم أنفقه

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says the person lied and spent nothing; whether he spent the money or not, God saw and knew the truth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي : كان كاذبا لم ينفق شيئا ، فقال الله تعالى : أيظن أن الله تعالى ما رآى ذلك منه

STUDYQURAN:90:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r1.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r1.claim: The question asks whether people think God will ask how they acquired and spent their wealth.
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r1.anchor: This verse asks, “Do people think that God will not ask how they obtained their wealth and how they spent it?”

STUDYQURAN:90:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r2.speaker: R, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r2.claim: Some apply the verse to a person who falsely claimed to have spent money for Islam.
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r2.anchor: Some say this refers to a specific individual who claimed to have spent money for Islam, though he had not spent anything

STUDYQURAN:90:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r3.speaker: Hadith
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r3.claim: A hadith says a servant will be questioned at Resurrection about lifespan, the source and use of wealth, and knowledge put into practice.
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r3.anchor: The servant does not move forward on the Day of Resurrection until he has been asked about three things

STUDYQURAN:90:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r4.speaker: Shiite version
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r4.claim: A Shiite version adds a fourth question about love for the Prophet's Household.
STUDYQURAN:90:7/r4.anchor: a Shiite version adds a fourth

TAB-FULL:v24p414/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p414/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p414/r1.claim: Qatāda says people are accountable for where their wealth came from and where they spent it.
TAB-FULL:v24p414/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {أيحسب أن لم يره أحد} [البلد: 7] : ابن آدم إنك مسئول عن هذا المال، من أين اكتسبته، وأين أنفقته

THALABI:v10p208/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r1.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p208/r1.claim: Muqātil says the passage was revealed about al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal: after being told to expiate a sin, he complained that conversion had consumed his wealth in expiations and expenses.
THALABI:v10p208/r1.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف

THALABI:v10p208/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v10p208/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads lubadan with a doubled bāʾ as the collective of labid and rākiʿ.
THALABI:v10p208/r2.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الباء على جمع لابد وراكع

THALABI:v10p208/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p208/r3.claim: Mujāhid reads lubadan with both lām and bāʾ rounded and light, as in the expressions ‘a heavy matter’ or ‘a man lying on his side.’
THALABI:v10p208/r3.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد بضم اللام والباء مخففا كقولك: أمر بكر ورجل جنب

THALABI:v10p208/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p208/r4.claim: The remaining readers use a light bāʾ with ḍamma on lām and fatḥa on bāʾ, either as plural of a heap or a non-derived singular.
THALABI:v10p208/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم اللام وفتح الباء مخففين، ولها وجهان

THALABI:v10p208/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p208/r5.claim: ‘Does he think no one saw him?’ may refer to God, or to Muḥammad knowing his expenditure; the man lied, having not spent everything he claimed.
THALABI:v10p208/r5.anchor: يعني الله سبحانه وقيل: محمد (عليه السلام) فيعلم مقدار نفقته، وكان كاذبا لم ينفق جميع ما قال

THALABI:v10p208/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
THALABI:v10p208/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatāda say he assumes no one will see him and ask where his money came from and where he spent it.
THALABI:v10p208/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة: أيظن أن لم يره أحد فيسأله عن هذا المال من أين اكتسبه

THALABI:v10p208/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r7.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p208/r7.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says no servant's feet move on Judgment Day until asked about life, the source and use of wealth, knowledge and its practice, and love for the Prophet's family; Ibn Khurja says he heard this report only from al-Haytham.
THALABI:v10p208/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تزول قدما العبد يوم القيامة حتى يسئل عن أربع

THALABI:v10p208/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r8.speaker: رجل من بني عامر عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p208/r8.claim: A man of Banū ʿĀmir reports the Prophet reciting ayahsabu with kasra on the sīn.
THALABI:v10p208/r8.anchor: أخبرني رجل من بني عامر عن أبيه قال: صليت خلف النبي صلى الله عليه فسمعته يقول: أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد

ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n5/r1.claim: The question asks whether a person thinks he is answerable to no one but himself.
ASAD-NOTES:90:5#n5/r1.anchor: Does he think that he is responsible to none but himself

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r1.claim: He assumes God did not see his deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r1.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: أيحسب أن لم ير الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r2.claim: He thinks God was unaware of what he did.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال مقاتل: أيحسب أن لم يطلع الله على

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r3.claim: The warning is that God saw him and will ask how he earned and spent his wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r3.anchor: أيظن أن الله لم يره، ولا يسأله عن ماله من

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r4.speaker: الكلبي، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r4.claim: He is lying about spending so much: God saw whether he spent anything, and al-Farra selects this interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p20/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان كاذبا، لم ينفق ما قال، فقال الله:

WAHIDI-QT:90:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:7/r1.claim: God saw his spending and knows how much he spent.
WAHIDI-QT:90:7/r1.anchor: قال الله تعالى { أيحسب أن لم يره أحد } في انفاقه فيعلم مقدار نفقته

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: The challenge resembles the rhetorical questions in 75:3 and 75:36.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza resumes the human-being statement at the introduction’s end and consists of two triplets marked by rhyme; the repeated third-person polemical questions formally unify them.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz, das pronominal an den ʾinsān-Spruch am Ende des Einleitungsgesätzes anknüpft, gliedert sich in zwei reimlich voneinander abgesetzte Dreiergruppen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.claim: The first triplet attacks possessiveness and imagined self-sufficiency apart from God, a stance called istaġnā in other early suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die erste Gesätzhälfte ist eine an 104 erinnernde Besitzpolemik; sie prangert jene menschliche Haltung vermeintlicher Selbstgenügsamkeit und Nicht-Angewiesenheit auf Gott an

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r3.claim: The questions ask whether anyone has power over the human being or sees him; their repeated opening and rhyme word make a clear verbal correspondence.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r3.anchor: Sie beginnen anaphorisch mit ʾa-yaḥsabu und tragen ʾaḥad im Reim.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r3.claim: God knows very well the purposes for which such people spend their wealth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:5/r3.anchor: Yüce Allah’ın böylelerinin hangi maksatlarla mal harcadıklarını gayet iyi bildiği

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r1.claim: The human assumes there will be no resurrection and that God cannot punish or requite him for what he has done.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r1.anchor: أنْ لن تقوم قيامة، ولن يقدر على الانتقام منه وعلى مكأفاته بما هو عليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r5.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r5.claim: The creator who gave humans strength is even more able than they are; this independently proves divine power, knowledge, and the ability to requite deeds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p257/r5.anchor: وجاء في (التبيان) : "ثم أنكر سبحانه على الإنسان ظنه وحسبانه أن لن يقدر عليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.speaker: التبيان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.claim: Al-Tibyan notes that lam marks the past, matching the past-tense boast: does the person think nobody saw what he spent and destroyed?
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r1.anchor: ثم وبخه بقوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ} وأتى ههنا بِلَمْ الدالة على المضي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r2.claim: The paired verses invoke God’s power and knowledge, with seeing signifying knowledge; these are the basis of the warning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p262/r2.anchor: أنه ذكر من صفات الله تعالى القدرةَ والعلم الذي دلت عليه الرؤية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.claim: The eyes given to the human directly answer his thought that nobody saw him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.anchor: ارتباط قوله تعالى: {أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ} بقوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p393/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p393/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p393/r1.claim: Seeing is more specific than knowing: the speaker imagines no one watched his spending, while God observes details and knows all creatures’ acts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p393/r1.anchor: الرؤية أهمّ وأخصّ من العلم وهناك فرق بين العلم بالشيء ورؤيته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r1.claim: Najd is the Qur’an’s distinctive word for a raised, difficult path; unlike the easy, well-traveled sabīl, it matches the sūra’s hardship and struggle.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r2.speaker: أغلب المفسرين
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r2.claim: Most commentators understand the two elevated paths as the path of good and the path of evil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r2.anchor: وأغلب المفسرين قالوا أنه يعني طريق الخير وطريق الشر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r3.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says one should not favor the path of evil over the path of good; the author calls this the closer interpretation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r3.anchor: وعن الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (لا يكن نجد الشرّ أحبّ إليكم من نجد الخير)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r4.claim: Guidance to the two paths means showing them, not guaranteeing a good destination: the road can lead to the Fire.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p394/r4.anchor: فهي تكون بمعنى الدلالة على الطريقين طريق الخير وطريق الشر

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r3.speaker: الأعمش
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the hāʾ in يره as quiescent; Ibn Jinnī says he has discussed this hāʾ treatment earlier.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p361/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الأعمش: "أن لم يره أحد5"، ساكنة الهاء.

QIRAAT-ER:90:7:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:90:7:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:90:7:1#1/r1.claim: The canonical form has kasra in the imperfect stem, preserving root and sense while changing the stem vowel from u to i.
QIRAAT-ER:90:7:1#1/r1.anchor: Canonical vowel variant with kasra in the imperfect stem; it preserves the same consonantal root

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r1.claim: Qatāda warns that a person will be questioned about where wealth was earned and spent.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r1.anchor: عبد الرزاق قال معمر تلا قتادة ﴿ أيحسب أن لم يره أحد ﴾ قال يا ابن آدم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r2.claim: A report from Abū Dharr says a servant's feet will not move until asked about four matters: lifespan, body, earnings, and where wealth was spent.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p373#5/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال معمر وسمعت رجلا يحدث عن أبي ذر قال لا يتحول قدما عبد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r1.claim: He may think nobody saw his spending, whether he sought public notice or spent in hostility to the Prophet; God observed it and will question and repay him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r1.anchor: أي حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاه الناس أو حرصا على معاداته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r2.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r2.claim: A prophetic report says a servant's feet will not move on Judgment Day until questioned about life, wealth and how it was earned and spent, and knowledge and its practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث لا تزول قدما العبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن أربع عن عمره فيم أفناه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r3.claim: Another reading takes “see” as “find” and the past-form negation as certain future: God will find and reckon with him on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى إن لم يجده أحد على أن المراد بالرؤية الوجدان اللازم له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says the boastful speaker lied and spent nothing; God saw what he did or did not do and can expose and recompense him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#2/r4.anchor: وعن الكلبي أن هذا القائل كان كاذبا لم ينفق شيئا فقال تعالى أيظن أن الله تعالى ما رأى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r1.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr and Qatada say the person thinks God neither sees him nor will ask where his wealth came from or where he spent it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير [وقتادة: أيظن] (1) أن الله لم يره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the man lied about how much he had spent, imagining God did not see the amount; the verse warns that God knows it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إنه كان كاذبا في قوله أنفقت كذا وكذا، ولم يكن أنفق جميع ما قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r2.claim: The boaster thinks no one saw his expenditure or will ask him about it, but God sees it and will judge it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r2.anchor: حين كان ينفق أو بعد ذلك فيسأله عنه، يعني أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يراه

BINTSHATI:v1p180/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r6.claim: The second rebuking question shifts from lan about future power to lam about past surveillance: the arrogant person’s entire past is already encompassed, after God’s control of his destiny was established.
BINTSHATI:v1p180/r6.anchor: التي تنصرف إلى الماضي فتقرر أن ماضي المغتر محسوب عليه

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.claim: Past tense with alam suits senses granted before the arrogant person feels powerful, while lan projects forward his deluded claim that no one will ever overpower him.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.anchor: أما حسبانه أن لن يقدر عليه أحد، فيأتي متأخراً بعد أن تطغيه القوة والمال

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.claim: The past and future references show that God governs the human being’s entire course, from creation to final return; the discussion invokes the opening revelation’s warning about human arrogance.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r6.anchor: بيان لمدى إحاطة الله بالإنسان مهما يبلغ من قوته وطغيانه

BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p183/r1.claim: God owns human destiny across past and future: He is the creator, and to Him is the return, as stated in the first revealed sūra.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r1.claim: The defiant person imagines no one saw his secret or public deeds, though God sees every part of his conduct and can undo its effects.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r1.anchor: في عمله هذا سره وجهره وجميع أمره

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r3.claim: The One who sees the person is God, exalted and mighty.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {أهلكت مالا لبدا} قال: أنفقت مالا في الصد عن سبيل الله {أيحسب أن لم يره أحد} قال: الأحد: الله عز وجل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r1.speaker: الكسائي عن حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r1.claim: Al-Kisai alone transmits Hamza's sukūn on the final hāʾ in these forms; Mujahid says no one else reported it from Hamza.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r1.anchor: وروى الفراء عن الكسائي عن حمزة أنه قرأ ﴿ أيحسب أن لم يره أحد ﴾ و ﴿ خيرا يره ﴾

TAB:90:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:90:7/r1.claim: The person who boasts of spending thinks no one saw him while he claims to spend his wealth.
TAB:90:7/r1.anchor: أيظنّ هذا القائل أهلكت مالاً لُبَدا أن لم يره أحد في حال إنفاقه ما يزعم أنه أنفقه

TAB:90:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:7/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:90:7/r2.claim: Qatada warns that a person will be questioned about where his money came from and where he spent it.
TAB:90:7/r2.anchor: عن قتادة أَيَحْسَبُ أنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أحَدٌ ابن آدم إنك مسئول عن هذا المال ، من أين اكتسبته ، وأين أنفقته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r1.claim: The description of a man whose property is shared by nearly everyone is neither a report about a known generous person nor a claim that he surpasses others in a gradable trait; it asks the listener to imagine the description and recognize its exact match.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r1.anchor: يقول للمخاطب : ضع في نفسك معنى قولك ' رجل مشروك في جل ماله '

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r2.claim: This rhetorical mode constructs in the mind something unseen and unknown, then treats it as though it were familiar and established.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r2.anchor: وأن يصور في خاطره شيئا لم يره ولم يعلمه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r3.claim: The relative pronoun alladhī often introduces this imagined description, as if the listener first posits something in thought and then names it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p147/r3.anchor: من ' الذي ' ؛ فإنه يجيء كثيرا على أنك تقدر شيئا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r1.claim: Al-aḥad and al-wāḥid are names for the starting point in number.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r2.claim: Ibn Faris equates الأحد with الواحد and says استأحد الرجل means that a man became isolated.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والأحد : بمعنى الواحد . واستأحد الرجل : انفرد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r3.claim: One Quranic referent of الأحد is God; the source cites the neighboring al-Balad verses about whether anyone can overpower or see the man.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p115/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الأحد في القرآن على أربعة أوجه : أحدها : الله عز وجل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r1.claim: Arabic may cast an important past event in the imperfect as a vivid, present scene, because listeners engage more with what seems before their eyes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r1.anchor: هذا يُسمّى حكاية الحال بمعنى إذا كان الحدث ماضياً وكان مهماً فإن العرب تأتي بصيغة المضارع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r4.speaker: الصحابي الذي قتل أبا رافع
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r4.claim: An unnamed Companion’s account of killing Abu Rafiʿ uses the imperfect فأضربه for the central blow, making the listener picture the action as it unfolds.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p867/r4.anchor: فناديت أبا رافع فقال نعم فأهويت عليه بالسيف فأضربه وأنا دهش

NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.claim: Twelve letters in twenty places depart from the regular rules; examples include fa-alqihi ilayhim and an lam yarahu.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r6.anchor: وعدته اثنا عشر حرفا في عشرين موضعا

NASHR:v2p148/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p148/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p148/r5.claim: The open أن لم is written separately throughout the Qurʾān, including the phrase in al-Balad 90:7.
NASHR:v2p148/r5.anchor: (وأن لم) المفتوح كتب مفصولا في جميع القرآن نحو ذلك أن لم يكن ربك

ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.claim: He should not think his deeds are hidden: watchers record what he does throughout life and preserve it until judgment.
ABUHAYYAN:90:6/r2.anchor: بل عليه حفظة يكتبون ما يصدر منه من عمل في حياته ويحصونه إلى يوم الجزاء

ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r1.claim: One view says the pronoun refers to one of Quraysh’s magnates.
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r1.anchor: وقيل : الضمير في { أيحسب } لبعض صناديد قريش .

ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r2.claim: Another identifies Abū al-Asad Usayd ibn Kilda, who stood on an ʿUkāẓ leather mat, dared people to move him, and could only be shifted in pieces.
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : هو أبو الأسد أسيد بن كلدة ، كان يبسط له الأديم العكاظي ، فيقوم عليه ويقول : من أزالني عنه فله كذا

ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r3.claim: Another view identifies al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : الوليد بن المغيرة . وقيل : الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل

ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.claim: Another view identifies al-Ḥārith ibn ʿĀmir ibn Nawfal, who sought the Prophet’s rulings on expiation and then boasted he had spent vast sums on expiations and liabilities.
ABUHAYYAN:90:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل ، وكان إذا أذنب استفتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فيأمره بالكفارة ، فقال : لقد أهلكت مالاً لبداً في الكفارات والتبعات

ALUSI:90:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:7/r1.claim: Whether he spent to display himself or out of hostility to the Prophet, God saw and watched him, and will question and requite him.
ALUSI:90:7/r1.anchor: أي حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاء الناس أو حرصاً على معاداته صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:90:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:7/r2.claim: An ungraded hadith cited here says a person’s feet will not move on Judgment Day until questioned about lifespan, wealth’s source and spending, and knowledge and its use.
ALUSI:90:7/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث «لا تزل قدما العبد يوم القيامة حتى يسأل عن أربع عن عمره فيم أفناه وعن ماله مم جمعه

ALUSI:90:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:7/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes ‘see’ as ‘find’ and lam as meaning lan, expressing certainty: God will find him on Judgment Day and reckon him for it.
ALUSI:90:7/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى أن لم يجده أحد على المراد بالرؤية الوجدان اللازم له ولم بمعنى لن

ALUSI:90:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI:90:7/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says the claimant lied and had spent nothing; the verse rebukes his assumption that God did not see whether he spent or not, since God knows the truth.
ALUSI:90:7/r4.anchor: وعن الكلبي أن هذا القائل كان كاذبا لم ينفق شيئاً فقال تعالى

ALUSI:90:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:7/r5.claim: The reminder of the two eyes follows to establish God’s power to requite and account for the person, as well as His knowledge of his state.
ALUSI:90:7/r5.anchor: وقرر سبحانه القدرة على مجازاته ومحاسبته والإطلاع على حاله

BAGHAWI:90:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:7/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
BAGHAWI:90:7/r1.claim: They explain the question as asking whether he thinks God did not see him or will not question where he acquired and spent his wealth.
BAGHAWI:90:7/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة : أيظن أن الله لم يره ،   ولا يسأله عن ماله من أين اكتسبه ،   وأين أنفقه ؟

BAGHAWI:90:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:7/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI:90:7/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says the man falsely boasts of spending more than he actually did, imagining God did not see and know the amount.
BAGHAWI:90:7/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي : إنه كان كاذباً في قوله أنفقت كذا وكذا ،   ولم يكن أنفق جميع ما قال

BAYDAWI:90:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:7/r1.claim: He imagines no one saw his spending, at the time or later to question him; God sees it and will reckon with him.
BAYDAWI:90:7/r1.anchor: حين كان ينفق أو بعد ذلك فيسأله عنه يعني أن الله سبحانه وتعالى يراه فيجازيه

BIQAI:90:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:7/r1.claim: No one escapes God's sight or insight in past deeds, private or public, and He can erase their effects.
BIQAI:90:7/r1.anchor: أي بالبصر ولا بالبصيرة في الزمن الماضي

BIQAI:90:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:7/r2.claim: The fourth carnal desire is to keep one's affairs and hidden intentions concealed; the verse warns against acting as if misdeeds are unwitnessed and urges care for one's lifetime.
BIQAI:90:7/r2.anchor: وهي أن تكون أموره مستورة فلا يظهر على غيبه أحد

BIQAI:90:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:7/r3.claim: All that eludes him from these desires remains out of reach; he seeks it through hardship and peril yet never obtains what satisfies him.
BIQAI:90:7/r3.anchor: وكل ما فاته من آثار هذه الشهوات الأربع

DURR:90:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:6/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR:90:6/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the One who sees him as God.
DURR:90:6/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : { أهلكت مالاً لبداً } قال : أنفقت مالاً

IBNASHUR:90:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:7/r1.claim: The question clause is an explicative supplement to ‘I spent much wealth’: the boaster supposes everyone believes him, though some know he lies.
IBNASHUR:90:7/r1.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { يقول أهلكت مالاً }

IBNASHUR:90:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:7/r2.claim: Zuhayr's verse supports the point that a person's character becomes known even when he thinks it is hidden.
IBNASHUR:90:7/r2.anchor: قال زهير : ومهما تكن عند امرىء من خليقة

IBNASHUR:90:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:7/r3.claim: The interrogative rebukes the boaster and implies that God knows his inner state and that his generosity claim is false.
IBNASHUR:90:7/r3.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار وتوبيخ وهو كناية عن علم الله تعالى بدخيلته وأن افتخاره بالكرم باطل

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.claim: The disbeliever's boast that he squandered much wealth is a lie; God saw and recorded his deed, so there is no basis for his false claim.
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r1.anchor: وكان قول هذا الكافر { أهلكت مالا لبدا } كذباً منه فلذلك قال تعالى

IBNATIYYA:90:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r2.claim: Those who read al-insān generically take the question to mean: does a person think no recording angels watch and count his deeds until Judgment?
IBNATIYYA:90:6/r2.anchor: ومن قال إن المراد اسم الجنس غير معين مفرد جعل قوله تعالى [ أيحسب أن لم يره أحد ] بمعنى : أيظن الإنسان أن ليس عليه حفظة يرون أعماله ويحصونها إلى يوم الجزاء ؟

IBNATIYYA:90:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:7/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA:90:7/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads lam yarah with a quiescent rāʾ to avoid the succession of vowel movements.
IBNATIYYA:90:7/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( لم يره ) بسكون الراء لتوالي الحركات

IBNKATHIR:90:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:7/r1.speaker: مجاهد وغيره من السلف
IBNKATHIR:90:7/r1.claim: The one who sees the person is God; other early authorities gave the same interpretation.
IBNKATHIR:90:7/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد : أي أيحسب أن لم يره الله عز وجل

KASHSHAF:90:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:7/r1.claim: While he spent to be seen and to boast, God saw him and kept watch over him.
KASHSHAF:90:7/r1.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رئاء الناس

KASHSHAF:90:7/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:7/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:7/r4.claim: One view identifies the person who thinks no one can overcome him as Abū al-Ashadd, a strong man who challenged others to remove him from a stretched hide and left only his footprints.
KASHSHAF:90:7/r4.anchor: هو أبو الأشد ، وكان قويا يبسط له الأديم العكاظي فيقوم عليه

KASHSHAF:90:7/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:7/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:7/r5.claim: Another view identifies him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
KASHSHAF:90:7/r5.anchor: وقيل : الوليد بن المغيرة «لبدا » قرىء بالضم

MAWARDI:90:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:7/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:90:7/r1.claim: Mujāhid takes the unseen witness to be God: does the person think God did not see him?
MAWARDI:90:7/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن لم يره الله ،   قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:90:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:7/r2.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:90:7/r2.claim: Ibn Shajara takes it to mean that no person saw what he spent.
MAWARDI:90:7/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن لم يره أحد من الناس فيما أنفقه ،   قاله ابن شجرة

MAWARDI:90:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:90:7/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:90:7/r3.claim: Māwardī also reads it as a threat: the person thinks his deed will not be exposed or punished; the two earlier readings instead charge him with denial.
MAWARDI:90:7/r3.anchor: ويحتمل وجهاً ثالثاً : أيحسب أن لم يظهر ما فعله أن لا يؤاخذ به ،   على وجه التهديد

NASAFI:90:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:7/r1.claim: He spent to show off and boast; God saw him and kept watch over him.
NASAFI:90:7/r1.anchor: حين كان ينفق ما ينفق رياء وافتخاراً يعني أن الله تعالى كان يراه وكان عليه رقيباً

QURTUBI:90:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:7/r1.claim: The question means: does he suppose nobody observed him? God knew what he did, so his claim to have spent the money was a lie.
QURTUBI:90:7/r1.anchor: " أيحسب " أي أيظن . " أن لم يره " أي أن لم يعاينه " أحد " بل علم اللّه عز وجل ذلك منه ، فكان كاذبا في قوله : أهلكت ولم يكن أنفقه

QURTUBI:90:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI:90:7/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a servant is questioned about his wealth, claims to have spent and given zakat, then is told he acted to be called generous and is sent to the Fire.
QURTUBI:90:7/r2.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة قال : يوقف العبد ، فيقال ماذا عملت في المال الذي رزقتك ؟ فيقول : أنفقته وزكيته . فيقال : كأنك إنما فعلت ذلك ليقال سخي

QURTUBI:90:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:90:7/r3.claim: Qatada says a person is accountable for where his wealth came from and how he spent it.
QURTUBI:90:7/r3.anchor: وعن سعيد عن قتادة : إنك مسؤول عن مالك من أين جمعت ؟ وكيف أنفقت ؟

QURTUBI:90:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r11.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI:90:7/r11.claim: A report says the Prophet read أيحسب with ḍamma on the sīn at both occurrences.
QURTUBI:90:7/r11.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم أنه كان يقرأ " أيحسب " بضم السين في الموضعين

QURTUBI:90:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:7/r12.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:90:7/r12.claim: Al-Hasan takes the speaker to mean: I have squandered much wealth, so who will hold me to account? Let me reckon it myself; God can in fact reckon with him and sees his conduct.
QURTUBI:90:7/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن : يقول أتلفت مالا كثيرا ، فمن يحاسبني به ، دعني أحسبه . ألم يعلم أن اللّه قادر على محاسبته ، وأن اللّه عز وجل يرى صنيعه
